 [Weather] Autumn Rain in Jeonnam-Gwangju Through Tomorrow... Temperatures to 'Plunge' Too
 by Min Chanki 
 Published 20 Oct.2026 17:09(KST) 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 Morning lows of 13 degrees Celsius... Strong winds will make it feel colder
 Autumn rain will continue across the Jeonnam-Gwangju region until dawn tomorrow, bringing the onset of a full-fledged cold spell.
 On the chilly morning of the 6th, people hurried across Gwanghwamun Square in Jongno-gu, Seoul, as cold weather gripped the nation. Yonhap News Agency
 View original image 
 According to the Gwangju Regional Meteorological Administration, rain will fall occasionally across the Jeonnam-Gwangju region through dawn on the 21st, with totals of around 5-30 mm. Even after the rain stops, scattered raindrops of less than 0.1 mm may fall in some areas from morning through daytime.
 Starting tomorrow afternoon, temperatures will plunge as cold air moves in strongly from the northwest. 
 The morning low on the 21st will be 13-16 degrees Celsius, and the daytime high will be 18-21 degrees, around average or slightly below. However, strong winds accompanying the cold air will make it feel much colder.
 On the 22nd, the morning low will drop sharply by around 5-10 degrees from tomorrow, to 5-10 degrees, while the daytime high will range from 16 to 18 degrees. The difference between daytime and nighttime temperatures is expected to widen to around 10 degrees, particularly inland.
 The Korea Meteorological Administration issued preliminary strong wind advisories for Yeosu, Yeongam, Hampyeong, Mokpo, Sinan, Jindo, Yeonggwang, Haenam, Muan, Heuksando and Hongdo, effective from dawn on the 21st, and for Geomundo, Chodo and Yeoseo Island in Wando, effective from the morning of the 21st.

 A Korea Meteorological Administration official said, "After the rain stops, temperatures will drop sharply, and very strong winds will blow, particularly along the coast. Please take thorough precautions to protect vessels engaged in offshore fishing and other facilities, and take special care of your respiratory health during the seasonal transition amid the sudden temperature changes."
